First listed: 2026-02-16 | Evaluation cutoff: 2026-11-10

## Source versions

- [YouTube: Daniel Guetta on the Guts of AI, Agentic AI & Why LLMs Hallucinate | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 46](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Rv_rPAQ3M9Q) - 2026-02-16
- [Substack: Daniel Guetta on the Guts of AI, Agentic AI & Why LLMs Hallucinate | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 46](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/daniel-guetta-on-the-guts-of-ai-agentic) - 2026-02-16

Earliest listed publication among matched versions, not proof of an unedited contemporaneous archive. Claim timestamps refer to the reviewed version.

## Summary

Eisman seeks a second technical view after Gary Marcus. Guetta argues that imperfect present-day AI can create value through representations, retrieval and tools without resolving AGI. The interview contains useful deployment distinctions, but its repeated full-context-recomputation and nearest-word explanations are technically misleading. Eisman leaves the industry return-on-investment verdict open until 2027-2028.

Empirical premises and forecasts are assessed separately. Guest assertions are not Eisman forecasts. Unverified magnitudes and causal attribution remain unresolved.

<a id="substack-203543819-c010"></a>
### 010. Each generated token requires reprocessing the entire previous conversation through the model from scratch, explaining high energy use.

**Wrong** | Daniel Guetta | explanation | major

[Source at 11:12-11:40](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/daniel-guetta-on-the-guts-of-ai-agentic) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

Standard KV caching avoids recomputing previous keys and values. Long context still costs memory and attention computation, but full from-scratch reprocessing on every token is not necessary.

Assessment test: Inspect the relevant original financial, operational or economic data and compare the claimed mechanism with competing explanations.

Further verification: Recheck the original data and subsequent realized outcomes.

- [How caching works](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/cache_explanation) (undated, inspected 2026-11-10): KV caching reuses previous tokens' attention keys and values during inference, avoiding full recomputation for every generated token. New queries still attend to cached context, which has memory and computation costs.

## Framework and tools

- Separate useful task economics from claims of general intelligence.
- Benchmark performance is specific to a task distribution.
- Data access, integration and action controls are deployment requirements.
- Lower coding cost does not automatically erase workflow and coordination moats.
- Use explicit cost and error budgets to evaluate imperfect tools.
- Eisman actively seeks a competing expert view and retains a 2027-2028 ROI horizon.

Tools and charts discussed, not a complete visual inspection:

- Learned embeddings and the Transformer architecture.
- KV caching as a correction to the inference-cost explanation.
- MMLU versus realistic work evaluations.
- External retrieval and multimodal representations.
- Reinforcement learning with human feedback and verifiable rewards.

## Source cautions

Steve Eisman interviews Columbia professor Daniel Guetta. Guest technical assertions and personal coding-view revisions remain guest claims. The host's acceptance of the inference-energy explanation is recorded separately.
- Every one of the 1,293 supplied normalized segments was read in full.
- The supplied publisher transcript contains repeated watermark-like lines and multi-second gaps, including parts of the travel and database examples and the closing disruption discussion. Read-complete refers to all available text, not a claim of complete audio recovery.
- SPEAKER_01 generally identifies Eisman and SPEAKER_02 Guetta, with occasional joined turns; the disclaimer is SPEAKER_00.
- The host describes Marcus's views to elicit a second opinion; they are not automatically Eisman predictions.
- Guetta qualifies his AGI skepticism and explicitly disclaims expertise about several markets; the host's closing summary is stronger than the guest's actual language.
- The old 5% enterprise-readiness estimate is explicitly described by the guest as outdated.
